newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to off.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to off.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.200 cent higher to 0.100 lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Reports that fed cattle trade finally developed late Thursday at $72 per cwt should prompt early demand in live cattle futures. Futures prices had slipped at times Thursday on concern packers may be able to purchase cattle at $71. The $72 sales confirm feedlots remain in control and live prices could rise to $73 next week, analysts said.
However, lower beef prices may weigh on sentiment.

Wholesale boxed beef prices were lower again Thursday, falling to three week lows and this may temper any expected gain from strong live markets. Evening up and spillover action from pork pits ahead of Friday afternoon's quarterly Hogs and Pigs report may also bring uneven trade at times, they said.
Feeder cattle were expected to show early resistance from the lower index and higher corn futures calls, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.07 at $63.48 per cwt.
